lines.text: But the same deprivation does something completely different to Aarav's friend Deepa.
She wants to become a doctor. Her family cannot afford it either. But Deepa does not let go. She becomes consumed.
I don't care how long it takes. Nothing else matters.
You haven't eaten properly in two days.
Elster calls this counteradaptive preference — the exact opposite of sour grapes. The forbidden fruit tastes sweetest.
Deepa inflates the value of medicine because it is denied. Same deprivation, opposite response. Neither is simply rational.
